value.name: Bánh chưng
value.text: Bánh chưng (literally "steamed cake") is a traditional Vietnamese dish which is made from glutinous rice, mung beans and pork, all wrapped in (Stachyphrynium placentarium) and tied tightly with strings (Maclurochloa sp.). It is traditionally eaten during Lunar New Year .

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4632245

ingredients: 1½ cups mung beans, washed and soaked in water for 4 hours, or better overnight
5½ cups sticky rice, washed and soaked in water for 4 hours, or better overnight, and seasoned with salt
2½ tsps black pepper, preferably freshly ground
1 kg banana leaves, fresh or thawed
instructions: To make the fillings for bánh chưng, soak the mung beans in water for at least 4 hours, or better overnight.
Place the mung beans in a pot and fill with water until covered.
Bring the pot to a boil and then reduce heat to a simmer.
Cook until the beans are soft and easily mashable for about 20 minutes.
Mash the beans into a paste. Season to taste with 1 tsp salt, stock powder, fried shallots, 1 tsp pepper and 1 tbsp vegetable oil.

For the meat, use both lean pork and pork fat. Cut them into large cubes, then season with ½ tsp salt and 1½ tsp pepper. Also add the minced shallots and 2 tbsps fish sauce. Mix well and let it marinate for a few hours.
Take about a cup of the mashed mung beans, spread it out on a thin plastic film, add a few pieces of lean pork and pork fat and shape it into a round or squared piece.
Tear the banana leaves into very large pieces, around 18 to 20 inches.

Lay out two sheets of partially overlapping banana leaves on a flat surface. Place a cup of sticky rice, which has been soaked in water overnight and seasoned with salt, at the center of the leaves. Place the fillings on top of the rice and then cover it up with another cup of sticky rice. Fold the leaves and wrap it up tightly like a present.

To prevent water penetrating into the cake during the boiling process, it is important to wrap up the cake two times. For the inner layer, make sure that the darker side of the banana leaf faces the rice so that it can tint the cake with a nice subtle green color later on. However, for the outer layer, the darker side of the banana leaf should face outside to give it a beautiful green package.
After the cake has been wrapped up, tie the cake tightly with twines.
Arrange the cakes tightly in a large stockpot and fill with water. Bring the stockpot to a boil and let it simmer until the cakes feel plump and the rice is congealed for about 6 to 8 hours.

To enjoy the cake, just removes the twines and unwrap the cake. Because the cake is sticky, it might be difficult to cut it with a knife. Cut the cake into wedges or slices using a thread or dental floss.

Bánh chưng is often eaten with pickled onions (dưa hành), pickled vegetables in fish sauce (dưa món), or dipped in sugar for a sweet treat. They can also be sliced, pan fried until golden, and served with sugar or sweet chili sauce.

value.name: Quick Sourdough Starter
value.text: This is a quick way to start a sourdough starter and is particularly useful for Amish friendship bread. Instead of relying on the wild yeast and bacteria that are naturally present in the air, it swaps in a commercial yeast. Because the commercial strains are very vigorous, it is unlikely that wild yeast will supplant them.

ingredients: 1 cup (240 ml) all-purpose flour or a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend
⅓ cup (240 ml) granulated cane sugar
2 tablespoon (15 ml) coconut oil, melted and cooled
instructions: Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, salt, and sugar in the large bowl.
Whisk together the almond milk, coconut oil, applesauce, molasses, and vanilla in the medium bowl.
Mix the wet with the dry ingredients successively.
Grease the baking pan and fill it with the batter.
Bake for 12 minutes at 190 °C (375 °F) or until it tests clean when a skewer is inserted into the center.
Cool and unmold the cake.

value.name: Date Syrup
value.text: Date syrup is a syrup used in various foods and drinks, both alcoholic and nonalcoholic. This recipe originates from Unicorns in the Kitchen.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4608740

ingredients: 1 cup (120 ml) Medjool dates, seeds removed
instructions: Bring the water to a boil, and pour it over the dates in a heat-proof bowl.
Let the dates soak for around half an hour.
Use a blender to purée the date-water mixture.
Transfer the mixture to a pot, and simmer over medium heat for 1 hour.
Remove the mixture from the heat and allow to cool to room temperature.
Strain the mixture through several layers of cheesecloth or a nut milk bag.

Return the strained liquid to a pot, and simmer until it reaches your desired syrup consistency. Keep in mind that it will thicken after cooling—if you have a thermometer, you can use it to monitor the sugar concentration, aiming for somewhere between 104–113°C (219–235°F).
Remove from the heat and allow to cool.

value.name: Date Soda
value.text: Date soda is a beverage made from date syrup and carbonated water.

instructions: Combine syrup and carbonated water until evenly mixed.
Serve cold.

value.text: Grenadine soda is a beverage made from grenadine syrup and carbonated water.

instructions: Combine grenadine and carbonated water until well-mixed.

value.name: Supercharger Tea
value.text: Supercharger tea is a variant of iced tea intended to give a sense of energy. The recipe is high in sugar and caffeine and thus best used before a busy day of work or study, but is easy to make.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4606564

instructions: Place tea bags in French press or coffee pot. Make sure to keep the strings taut to prevent the paper weights from falling in.
Pour the hot water into French press. Place lid on top, with a tight grip on the paper weights.
Let the tea steep for 5 minutes.
If using a French press, slowly push the plunger onto the bags, again with a tight grip on the paper weights.
Take off the lid, scoop the teabags out, and gently squeeze the brew from the bags before disposing of them.
Add sweetener and stir thoroughly.
Let tea cool to room temperature. Serve over ice, or place open pot in freezer for 70 minutes for quicker cooling. Stir in milk or citrus juice before serving.

value.name: Breakfast Dürüm
value.text: Dürüm is a Middle Eastern fast food similar to a wrap. The variation here combines a modified spinach mushroom omelet recipe, hash browns, hummus, and beef steak, all within an earthy, nutty wheat flatbread known as “lavash” or “yufka”, for an intensely spicy and greasy portable breakfast meal.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4639030

ingredients: 1 large sheet of lavash or yufka flatbread
4 tbsp butter or olive oil, divided
½ cup thinly sliced baby bella or Crimini mushrooms
5 thin slices cooked beef sirloin or flank
instructions: Brush the flatbread with the tablespoon of water to keep it soft. Toast the bread using a skillet or in a toaster oven until brown on edges. Set aside.

Combine the grated potato with half the hot water in a bowl. Let sit for 3 minutes, then stir thoroughly and drain the water from the bowl. Repeat this process with the remaining hot water, then drain the potatoes in a colander. Shake gently in a horizontal motion to remove excess starch and water, then set aside to dry.
Sauté the mushrooms in 1 tbsp butter. Add spinach, and cook on medium heat until slightly wilted.

Whisk together the eggs, seasonings and milk, then pour over the spinach and mushrooms. When the eggs are half-set, sprinkle the cheddar on top, then fold the omelet in half and remove from the skillet.

Heat the remaining butter in the skillet. Turn the heat to high, then add the potatoes, onions, and steak, evenly and fully covering the bottom of the skillet. Season to taste, then let them sear to your desired brownness and crunch, taking care to turn them over. Remove from the heat.

Assemble the dürüm by laying the bread sheet flat, with the longer edges to the left and right sides. Spreading the hummus evenly on the half of the bread farthest from you. Pile the potato mixture and the omelet evenly on the nearest half. Pinch and fold the nearest edge over, then roll into a 5-cm (2-inch) thick cylinder and serve.

value.name: Kuku Sabzi with Potato Slices
value.text: Kuku sabzi is a Persian dish made of eggs and herbs. The panoply of leafy fragrances in this variant recipe cuts into the starchy potato flavor, an influence from the tortilla española.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4608918

ingredients: ½ bunch fresh cilantro, finely chopped
½ bunch fresh dill, finely chopped
1 tbsp finely chopped dried fenugreek leaves
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, salt, pepper, nutmeg and milk, until glossy and even.
Rinse the potato slices and transfer to a bowl. Cover with hot water and soak for 10 minutes to remove excess starch. Drain away the excess water.
Fry the potato slices in a skillet with the paprika and half of the butter until the potatoes are soft, tender and brown. Tilt the pan in a circular motion to coat potatoes evenly.
Add the onions and herbs and stir thoroughly, then sauté until onions are soft and translucent.
Add the remaining half of the butter to the skillet. Stir contents thoroughly to evenly coat with the fat, then lower the heat.
Pour the beaten eggs into the skillet, tilting the skillet in a circular motion until vegetables are bound with the eggs. Heat until the eggs have set on the sides.

Using the spatulas and taking care not to break it, fold the edges of the kuku sabzi a centimeter toward the center, forming a large disk with a brown crust on the bottom. Turn the heat off and let skillet cool slightly.
Place a plate on the skillet and carefully flip the skillet over to unmold the disk of eggs.
Return the egg disk to the skillet, with the uncooked side on the bottom and the crust on top. Turn the heat to high, cook until the crust forms on the bottom, and remove from the heat.
Using the spatula, pull and lift the browned kuku sabzi off the skillet, onto plate, and serve.

value.name: Veggie Pizza
value.text: This veggie mini-pizza is a spin on pizza Margherita, providing a wider array of nutrients and flavors.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4610465

ingredients: 1 pre-made pizza crust, rolled to 30 cm (12 inches) across
½ ea. green bell pepper, de-seeded and thinly sliced
½ cup thinly sliced baby bella mushrooms
4½ tbsp pitted and sliced black olives
instructions: Preheat oven to 240° C (450° F / Gas 9).
Brush the dough surface with olive oil.
Ladle the sauce over the dough, spreading it evenly.
Distribute the cheeses evenly over the crust.

Lay the toppings evenly over the cheese. If needed, press toppings down with a utensil to provide clearance from the oven ceiling. If desired, top the vegetables with extra cheese and sauce to hold vegetables down.
Bake pizza in oven until crust edges are deep dark brown (roughly 15 minutes for pre-made crust, much longer for freshly made dough).
Take pizza out of oven and let cool.

value.name: Fribourg Omelet
value.text: A Fribourg omelet is a mix of eggs, crunchy greens, and ham, with the Swiss canton of Fribourg’s native Gruyère cheese adding an acidic punch to bind the flavors together.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4608896

ingredients: 3 thin slices of ham, cut in small squares
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, salt, pepper, milk and nutmeg, until even and glossy.
Place half the butter in the skillet on medium heat. Swirl the pan to coat evenly with butter.
Add ham and cook until deep brown.
Stir in kale for 30 seconds, or until slightly wilted but still crunchy. Set aside the ham and greens.
Add the remainder of the butter to the skillet over low heat.
Pour egg mixture into the skillet, moving skillet to create a flat, even layer. Heat until the eggs have begun to set, with some fluff on top.
Scatter the ham and kale evenly over the top of the eggs.
Lay the Gruyère slices over the open omelet. Heat until the edges of the cheese have melted slightly.
Gently push the edges of the omelet less than half a centimeter toward the center of the skillet with two spatulas, making sure not to break it. Turn the heat off.
Use the spatulas to lift half the omelet and fold over the other half. Move the entire omelet carefully onto a plate and serve.

value.name: Spinach Mushroom Omelet
value.text: This spinach mushroom omelet is an American diner-style breakfast dish that provides a creamy mix of fresh vegetable taste and sharp cheddar.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4606145

ingredients: ⅔ cup baby bella mushrooms, thinly sliced
½ ea. large red onion, diced
½ cup shredded aged cheddar cheese
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, salt, pepper, nutmeg and milk, until even and glossy.
Heat the skillet over medium heat. Add half the butter, tilting the skillet in a circular motion to coat evenly.
Add paprika, mushrooms, and onions, and sauté until lightly browned.
Add spinach and toss for 30 seconds, or until slightly wilted, but still crunchy. Remove the vegetables from the heat and set aside.
Add the remaining half of the oil or butter to the pan over medium heat, and coat evenly. Lower the heat.
Pour the egg mixture into the skillet, swirling the pan to ensure an even, creamy layer of eggs. Heat until the eggs have begun to set, with some fluff on top.
Top the egg layer with the vegetables, distributing the vegetables evenly. Sprinkle the cheese evenly on top.
Gently push the edges of the omelet half a centimeter toward the center of the skillet with two spatulas, making sure not to break it. Turn the heat off.
Use the spatulas to carefully lift/pull half the omelet off the skillet and fold it over the other half. Carefully move the entire omelet onto a plate and serve.

value.name: Steak and Wine Pie
value.text: This steak and wine pie is a variation on the Steak and Ale Pie recipe, one with a richer and more fruity sauce and a more crumbly, stiffer crust.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4606171

ingredients: 3 tbsp butter or margarine, cut into small cubes
¼ cup red wine or lemon juice
½ stalk celery, sliced ⅛ inch thick
⅓ whole carrot, sliced ⅛ inch thick, then cut into semicircles
instructions: Combine the flour, salt, and Italian seasoning in a shallow bowl, and mix to distribute well. Mix in the butter until solid, firm dough lumps form. If mixing by hand, pinch and clasp them together until a ball can be formed.
Dust a work surface and the dough ball with a little flour to prevent sticking. Flatten dough with a rolling pin until it forms a thin disk large enough to be draped over the pie plate or bowl.
Freeze the dough for 20 minutes, or for the duration of filling prep and cooking.
Combine the oil, wine, and soy sauce to make a marinade. Submerge the beef in the marinade, and let this marinate in the fridge for 24 hours.
Remove the meat from the marinade, and slice it ¼ inch thick.
Heat the saucepan over high heat, then add the butter and let it melt.
Add the sliced beef to the saucepan. Sauté, stirring, until browned all over.
Add bay leaf, thyme, basil, celery, onion, and carrot. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until onions and celery are soft.
Scrape some of the fond off the pan bottom without taking it out, if possible. Stir in the wine, Worcestershire sauce, and gravy granules for 1 minute
Turn heat to low, stir in ketchup, and cover the pan. Cook until stew volume is reduced by a third to half and liquids are beginning to thicken.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from the heat, and discard the bay leaf.
Pour filling into the pie plate or bowl.
Cover with the pie crust disk and press around edges to seal. The dough falling apart is acceptable as long as it retains an amount of crunch or flakiness.
Bake at 445 °F (230 °C / Gas 8) for 10 to 15 minutes or until top crust turns medium brown. Handle with care.

value.name: Holiday Soda
value.text: This holiday soda differs from anything you will find in a can and is perfect for the holiday season. It derives from a Flavor Lab recipe.

ingredients: ½ cup (120 ml) edible pine needles (preferably Douglas fir)
Peel from 3 clementine oranges (or a similar easy-to-peel variety such as tangerines)
instructions: Wash the pine needle branch and clementines.
Remove the pine needles from the branches and peel the clementines.

Mix the pine needles and clementine peels with the sugar in a container, and let this sit in the fridge for 24 hours. The sugar will extract the liquid from the citrus peels and produce a syrupy liquid.
Boil the cinnamon sticks, cloves, and cardamom pods in the water.
Pour the warm water with boiled spices into the container with pine needles and peels.
Mix the ingredients together and strain the mixture.
To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

value.name: Cassava Pone
value.text: Cassava pone is a dessert originating in the Caribbean. This recipe is modified from one by Alica's Pepperpot.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

ingredients: 3 lbs (1.36 kg) raw cassava, peeled and grated
½ tsp (2.5 ml) ground black pepper
4 tbsp (60 ml) melted butter or coconut oil
3 cups (720 ml) unsweetened evaporated milk or coconut milk
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Combine all the ingredients together, mixing well to incorporate.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish.
Bake the cassava pone for 60 minutes until firm and golden.

value.name: Jamaican Sorrel Soda
value.text: Jamaican sorrel soda is a traditional Jamaican carbonated drink consisting of sweetened hibiscus tea with added ginger.

ingredients: 3 hibiscus (roselle) tea bags or 3 tsp (15 ml) dried hibiscus
6 ea. ¼ in (0.67 cm) cubes of ginger (optional) (optional)
instructions: Combine the water, hibiscus, and ginger in a pot. Boil for about 15 minutes.
Remove and discard the hibiscus and ginger.
Stir the sugar into the liquid, and simmer until you have about 5 oz (150 ml) syrup.
Remove from the heat and let cool.
To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of sparkling water.

value.name: Fermented Soda
value.text: This recipe uses premade extracts and fermentation to make a carbonated beverage. It is adapted from an online blog.

ingredients: ⅛ tsp (0.625 ml) champagne yeast or 2 tsp (10 ml) kefir grains
instructions: Sterilize all your equipment before beginning.
Combine all of the ingredients in a container suitable for fermentation. Note that gas will be produced during the fermentation.
Put the container in a warm place, and allow it to ferment for 3 days.
If desired, strain the finished product. Store in the fridge.

value.name: Soda from Extract
value.text: If you drink a lot of soda, host many parties with soda, or own a carbonating machine, you can save money by using generic soda extracts. Making soda from extract often costs less than a third of the price of purchasing soda in bulk. This recipe is adapted from Cartoon Cuisine.

instructions: Boil the soda extract, water, and sugar together to make a syrup of about 10 oz (300 ml).
Mix the syrup with the carbonated water to make the finished soda.

value.name: Kendal Mint Cake
value.text: Confections | England cuisine | Holiday

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

instructions: Grease a square baking tin with vegetable oil.
Combine the sugar, glucose, and water in a saucepan over low heat. Stir periodically until the sugar dissolves.
Increase the heat to medium-high, and put a candy thermometer into the mixture. Cook, without stirring, until the mixture reaches about 150°C (300°F).

Remove the pan from the heat, and thoroughly stir in the peppermint extract. Continue stirring for several minutes until the mixture becomes cloudy/opaque and slightly thickened, but still pourable and spreadable.
Pour the sugar mixture into the prepared baking tin. Let rest for 30 minutes to cool and partially set.
Use a sharp knife to score the confection into squares or rectangles as desired. This makes it easier to break the confection into individual pieces after it sets fully.
Transfer the baking tin to the refrigerator, and chill for at least 2 hours to fully set the confection.
Remove the confection from the baking tin, and break into individual pieces.

value.name: Grenadine
value.text: Grenadine is a pomegranate syrup used in various drinks, both alcoholic and nonalcoholic. This recipe originates from a Reddit thread.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4607711

instructions: Mix the juice and sugar in a pot or saucepan.
Boil the juice and sugar, stirring constantly, until it becomes a thick and viscous syrup resembling dark honey.
Remove from the heat, and let it cool.
Let it cool.

value.name: Baklava II
value.text: Baklava is a Mediterranean dessert consisting of layers of phyllo dough interspersed with crushed nuts and soaked in sweet syrup.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4629321

ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) nuts (any type, but preferrably pistachios or walnuts)
instructions: Combine the nuts and cinnamon in a blender. Blend the nuts into a fine powder, being careful not to form a paste.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, then set aside.
Line a baking pan with parchment paper.
Count the number of sheets of phyllo dough and divide it by eight. Arrange one-eighth of the sheets in the bottom of the pan, on the parchment paper.
Divide the chopped nuts into seven equally sized portions.
Brush the phyllo dough with melted butter, and evenly distribute one portion of chopped nuts over the dough.
Arrange another eighth of the phyllo sheets on top of the nut layer.
Repeat the buttering and layering of nuts and phyllo until you have used up all the phyllo sheets and chopped nuts.
Using a sharp knife, radially cut the baklava into eight equally sized portions shaped like the British flag.
Bake the baklava for 25 minutes at 350°F (180°C). Remove from the oven, and let cool slightly.

Mix the vanilla extract, honey, sugar, and water in a clean saucepan. Boil over medium heat until it becomes a very thick and viscous syrup of slightly over 1 cup (240 ml). Remove from the heat, and let cool slightly.
Pour the syrup on top of the baked baklava, coating each portion of the baklava evenly with syrup.
Let everything cool fully before serving.

value.name: Langar Dal
value.text: Langar dal is a dish consisting of stewed dal (split lentils) served at many gurdwaras and mosques.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4597437

instructions: Rinse the dal three times and strain out the water.
Chop the onion into small cubes about 1 cm on each side.
Put the ghee in a pressure cooker and let it melt with the lid off.
Add the onions into the pot and sauté them for three minutes.
Add the turmeric powder to the pot and mix it well with the onions and ghee.
Add the dal, water, and salt.
Close the lid and seal the valve.
Pressure cook for 12 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally.
Enjoy!

value.name: Communion Wafers
value.text: Communion Wafers — a recipe imported from the Wikibooks Cookbook.

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4597328

instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Knead together the water and flour in a bowl to get a smooth dough.
Divide the dough into 4 equally sized portions.
Divide each of the 4 equally sized portions into four smaller portions for a total of 16 portions.
Roll each of the 16 small portions into small balls.
Flatten each of the small portions into small, thin, flat disks. If desired, use a butter knife to cut a small cross onto each wafer.
Bake the wafers for 3 minutes.
Take the wafers out of the oven and flip them over using a spoon or chopstick.
Bake the wafers for another 3 minutes.
Take the wafers out of the oven and let them cool.

value.name: Cherry Soda
value.text: A cherry soda is a soda flavored with cherries.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4598654

instructions: Combine the water, cherries, and sugar in a pot.
Boil the mixture until it becomes a thick syrup.
Strain the mixture, and discard the solids. This should yield about 5 oz (150 ml) syrup.
To make the finished soda, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

value.name: Herbal Energy Drink
value.text: An energy drink is a heavily caffeinated soft drink. This recipe contains a lot of caffeine, citrus, and herbs. This recipe originates from Flavorlab.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4601583

instructions: Combine the lemon and orange zests with the sugar, rubbing the sugar into the peels to extract the oils. Let this mixture rest in the fridge for 24 hours to infuse.
Bring the water to a boil, then stir in the sugar-zest mixture, lemon juice, licorice root, ginger, and ginseng. Boil until you get a thick syrup.
Strain the syrup and discard the solids. This should yield approximately 5 oz (150 ml) syrup.
Mix the caffeine, B vitamin complex, and taurine into the syrup.
To make the final energy drink, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

value.name: Citrus Energy Drink
value.text: An energy drink is a heavily caffeinated soft drink. This recipe contains a lot of caffeine and citrus. This recipe has been modified from a discussion at Stack Exchange.

ingredients: ½ ea. lemon, zested in strips and juiced
½ ea. lime, zested in strips and juiced
½ ea. orange, zested in strips and juiced
instructions: Combine the citrus zests and sugar, rubbing the sugar into the peels to extract the oils. Let this mixture rest in the fridge for 24 hours to infuse.
Combine the sugar-zest mixture with the citrus juices and caffeine. Stir well to dissolve the sugar and get a syrup.
Strain the syrup—this should yield approximately 5 oz (150 ml) syrup.
To make the finished beverage, mix 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

value.name: Cola III
value.text: Cola is a type of soda that flavored with citrus and spices. The word "cola" derives from kola nuts, a plant originating in West Africa and originally used as a source of caffeine to make this soda. Most modern recipes do not contain kola nuts.

ingredients: ¾ tsp (3.75 ml) 150+ proof unflavored food-grade spirit OR a mixture of ½ tsp (2.5 ml) water with ¼ tsp (1.25 ml) food-grade gum arabic
1 drop petit grain (lemon leaf and twig oil)
¾ tsp (3.75 ml) strained lime juice
instructions: Combine the spirits and oils together in a small cup, mixing well. Set aside.
Combine the phosphoric acid, caramel color, lime juice, water, and sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then boil until it becomes a thick syrup.
Remove the syrup from the heat, and stir in the caffeine and oil mixture. Let cool.
To make the finished soda, combine 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

value.text: Cola is a type of soda that flavored with citrus and spices. The word "cola" derives from kola nuts, a plant originating in West Africa and originally used as a source of caffeine to make this soda. Most modern recipes do not contain kola nuts.

ingredients: 2 oz (60 ml) 150+ proof unflavored spirit OR a mixture of 10 tsp (50 ml) water with 2 tsp (10 ml) gum arabic
⅔ cup (160 ml) water, heated to 122°F (50°C)
4 drops tea extract or a mixture of 2 parts water to 1 part matcha
instructions: Combine the spirit or gum arabic water and oils together in a small cup, mixing well. Set aside.

Combine the hot water, caffeine, caramel coloring, green tea extract, vanilla extract, lime juice, citric acid, sugar, and ¼ tsp (1.25 ml) of the oil mixture in a heat-safe container. Stir well to dissolve and make a syrup.
To make the finished soda, combine 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

value.name: Seblak
value.text: Seblak is a traditional snack from Sunda. This food is commonly found in West Java Province, especially in Bandung, Garut, and Tasikmalaya. It is made mainly from crackers with kencur (aromatic ginger) and chili as the main spices. Seblak is well-known for its spicy taste and easy preparation.

ingredients: 1/4 kg of boiled chicken meat (cut into small pieces)
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients.
Blend kencur (aromatic ginger), shallots, and garlic. Add a little salt.
Blend the chili separately.
Heat the oil in a pan.
Sauté the blended kencur, shallots, and garlic until fragrant and cooked.
Add the blended chili, then stir until it smells fragrant.
Next, pour in the water.
Add salt, chicken broth powder, and sugar to taste.
Put in the crackers and boiled chicken pieces, then stir until cooked.
Add the instant noodles, and stir again until everything is well-cooked.
Pour it into a bowl according to your preferred portion.
Seblak is ready to serve.

value.text: This prickly pear soda is popular in Mexico and the Southwestern United States.

instructions: Remove the peel from the prickly pears, cut them into small pieces about 0.5 x 0.5 in (1.25 x 1.25 cm), and remove the seeds.
Combine the fruit flesh, water, and agave nectar in a saucepan.
Boil the mixture until it becomes very thick, then strain it to get approximately 5 oz (120 ml) of syrup.
Make the finished soda by combining 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.

value.text: Sarsaparilla had significant popularity in the United States during the 19th century, but its popularity has faded more recently. This recipe is modified from Seed to Pantry School.

value.text: A pepper soda is a soda flavored with multiple fruits and spices. This recipe does not contain peppers; rather, the name derives from Dr. Pepper. This recipe has been modified from one by Youtube channel xoxo cooks.

instructions: Combine the water, prunes, ginger, cherries, zest, mint, anise, allspice, cloves, coriander, vanilla, and sugar in a saucepan.
Boil the mixture until it becomes a thick syrup.
Strain the syrup, discarding the solids, and stir in the caffeine. You should have about 5 oz (150 ml) syrup.

instructions: Remove the zest from the lemons and limes in strips, leaving behind the bitter white pith.

instructions: Heat up some oil in a pan over medium heat.
On a cutting board, with two tortillas, place a slice of deli ham and then queso fresco in the middle, and place another tortilla on top.
When the oil is hot, place the raw sincronizada on the pan and let the first side brown for a few minutes until the outside becomes crispy.

value.text: The origin of this particular recipe for lamb kofta is uncertain; this version is a family-developed recipe, though the ingredients match other recipes found online (e.g. ), which are cited as Moroccan. It is intended to be cooked via open flame or coals as opposed to in a pan.

ingredients: 3 oz lamb or other solid and flavorful fat (optional), chopped
1 ea white or yellow onion, minced or grated
instructions: Preheat a broiler or grill to moderate-high heat.
Combine all the ingredients in a mixing bowl. Use your hands to mix just until everything is combined and evenly distributed.
Use a spoon or your hands to scoop out portions of approximately 2–3 tablespoons. Use your hands to shape the meat mixture into oblong shapes about 2–3 inches (5–8 cm) in length.

If using an oven broiler, transfer the kofta onto a rack over a rimmed baking sheet to catch the drippings, and place them under the broiler. If grilling, arrange the kofta directly on the grill rack.
Broil or grill for a handful of minutes on each side, flipping halfway. You're looking for the outside to be slightly browned, and the inside should be cooked through but not dry.
Remove from the heat, and set aside to cool slightly before serving.

value.name: Creamy Tomato and Bean Soup
value.text: This recipe for creamy tomato bean soup uses mostly canned ingredients which means that it is faster to prepare than if using fresh tomatoes and dry beans. This blended soup is vegetarian and hearty enough to be eaten as a main course in a meal. This soup can also be made vegan by omitting the cream cheese.

ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil or neutral cooking oil
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) white beans, with liquid
5–10 cloves garlic (according to preference), peeled and cut in half
2 leaves fresh sage, torn in half by hand
2 cans (30 oz / 850 g) crushed or diced tomatoes
10–20 leaves of fresh basil, chiffonaded or torn to strips by hand
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat for about 30 seconds or until it begins to shimmer.
Add onions to the large pot of oil, and season with salt and pepper. Cook about 2 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Add the beans with their liquid, garlic, oregano, and sage. Simmer for 3–5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, red pepper, and water. Simmer an additional 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat, stir in the cream cheese. and break up any large piece with the stirring utensil.
Let the soup cool for 1–2 minutes, then use either a blender or stick blender to purée the soup.
Return the puréed soup to the stove at the lowest heat setting for an additional 10–15 minutes, stirring often to prevent burning.
Just before serving, stir in fresh basil leaves, reserving a handful to garnish each bowl.

value.name: Adobo Chicken (Philippine)
value.text: Adobo chicken is the most indigenous in the Philippines. It has evolved over the centuries to prepare foods that won't spoil easily in a tropical climate. The vinegar gives it a tangy taste and acts as a preservative. Each region has its own version, but pork and/or chicken are most commonly used. The steps below are the traditional way of making adobo. The soy sauce gives it a savoury taste.

ingredients: 6–8 chicken pieces, preferably legs and wings
⅓ cup (80 ml) vinegar made from coconut juice (as a variant, try balsamic vinegar)
½ tsp (2.5 ml) freshly cracked (not ground) black peppercorns
instructions: Put chicken, garlic, peppercorn, soy sauce and vinegar in a pan and bring to a boil.
When chicken is cooked, put chicken pieces in a colander and drain. Put aside the pot with soy sauce and vinegar.
When chicken pieces are no longer draining, fry them in hot oil at medium heat. Have a cover ready for splatters.
Sear the chicken, browning on all sides.
Put chicken pieces back in the pot with soy sauce and vinegar and bring to simmer. Add 1–2 pieces of bay leaf.

Cook until the sauce has largely evaporated; some take this to an extreme and cook until the sauce has thickened and adhered to the chicken, which begins to make a popping noise due to the high, direct heat.
Serve over hot steamed rice. May be eaten with tomato slices in fish sauce, tapsilog, soy sauce, vinegar, hotdog, etc.

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Whisk together the flours, sugars, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
Whisk together the mashed banana, egg, buttermilk, melted butter, and olive oil.
Add dry ingredients to the wet, and mix just until combined. Over-mixing will make them tough.

If needed, prepare the muffin tins by greasing them or lining them with liners (see notes).
Divide the batter between the prepared muffin cups, filling each cup about ⅔ full.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until cooked through—a tester inserted into the center should come out clean.

value.name: Tall Quiche Shell
value.text: This is a tall quiche shell as used in quiches served at Thomas Keller's restaurant, Bouchon. You can find the full version in his book, Bouchon. This version is brief, for reference, and the amount of water added has been increased slightly to make the dough easier to work with and more resilient. You can use less water; just be careful as you transfer and press the dough into the quiche ring.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4597429

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour (you can use whole grain, but softer wheat is better here)
8 oz chilled unsalted butter, cut into ¼ inch cubes
instructions: Combine the salt and half the flour in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment.
Add the butter, and mix on medium speed until the butter blends into the flour.
Add the rest of the flour, and mix for a few seconds on low speed.
Add the ice water and mix just until blended. You don't want to develop gluten here—you just want nice butter layers.
Remove the dough from the mixer. If desired, make a few random folds of it with your hand, not kneading but creating some layers that might flake during baking.
Pat dough into an 8 inch disk, wrap in tightly in plastic wrap, and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and put the quiche ring on top

Roll out the dough evenly until it's 14 inches in diameter and about 3/16 inch thick. A thinner shell can be done, but it will tear more easily, and patching tears is tricky. You can generously dust with flour as you're rolling.

Loosely roll the dough around your rolling pin, and center it over the quiche ring. Carefully working in a circle, tuck in the dough to make an even-bottomed, even-walled shell. Wrap the excess dough around the outside of the ring and press it down there, but keep it thick around the top of the ring. This will keep the dough from sagging or tearing around the top as it bakes. This step is the tricky one, so take your time and tuck the shell well into all the gaps, patching it smoothly anywhere it tears and pressing it even wherever there are thick folds. Along the outside of the ring, cut any dough that reaches down more than 1.25 inches. You can use this to patch any tears later.
Cover with plastic wrap and chill in the fridge for at least an hour.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.

Line the shell with parchment paper, and fill with baking beans or anything heavy to weigh it down, like uncooked rice. If you use baking beans, it takes a lot, so you can put fewer beans in the middle and push them up against the sides.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the parts of the crust that are showing on the outside are nice and golden brown.
Remove the parchment and weights, and patch any tears in the shell with the reserved dough from before. Be careful not to burn yourself on the hot ring.
Bake for another 15–20 minutes until the bottom is golden brown as well. Here, you can patch again, but take time to smooth the new dough into the dough below it or the patch won't hold very well.
Cool completely, and use as directed in your recipe.

value.name: Quiche Lorraine
value.text: This is a tall fluffy custard quiche as served at Thomas Keller's restaurant, Bouchon. This version is brief and slightly modified with less filling and more custard; you can find the full version in Keller's Bouchon cookbook.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4536093

ingredients: ¾ lb pork belly, skinned and cut into lardons 1½ x ⅜ inches
¼ tsp fresh ground black pepper
1 tall quiche shell, baked as directed in a 9x2-inch quiche ring on parchment
½ cup grated Comté or Emmentaler cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake pork belly lardons on baking sheet for 20–25 minutes. The fat should be rendered, but the pork should not be crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Lower oven heat to 325°F (163°C).
Add onion confit, pork, salt, pepper, and thyme to the frying pan over medium heat. Allow to warm up for 4 minutes. Drain on paper towels.
Arrange ¼ cup cheese and half the pork mixture in the bottom of the quiche shell.

Pour half the quiche batter into the shell, and check for leaks. If the shell is leaking a tiny bit or not at all, you can continue; if it's leaking a lot, it's best to bake the mixture in a casserole dish and serve the crust on the side.
Sprinkle the rest of cheese evenly over the filling, then top with the remaining pork mixture.
Add enough quiche batter to fill the rest of the crust without spilling. You may not need all of it.

Bake the quiche for about 90 minutes, checking every so often. The quiche is done when it's browned on top and it jiggles slightly like a properly set custard when you shake the pan. If it still looks quite liquid, it probably needs more time. If it's hard, puffed up a lot, and doesn't really jiggle, it might be overbaked. Adjust the time and temperature accordingly for your oven.
Cool completely at room temperature, then chill in the fridge at least overnight and up to 3 days.

Cut the excess crust off the top of the quiche ring, then run a paring knife carefully between the ring and the crust to separate them. Remove the ring, then slice the quiche. Serve at room temperature or warm up for 15 minutes at 350–375°F.

value.name: User:Cnrowley/Nanaimo Bars II
value.text: This recipe adapts the classic Canadian dessert recipes for Nanaimo bars to have reduced white sugar and saturated fat, replacing the coconut in the base with rolled oats and sunflower seeds. The sweet custard layer is replaced with a lightly sweetened greek yogurt layer.

parseFlags.detail: For best results, allow the dish to set by sitting in the fridge for 8 hours (overnight). To serve, cut into bars using a sharp knife dipped in warm water for clean edges.

ingredients: ½ cup sunflower seeds chopped to medium coarseness
2 tbsp custard powder (or substitute 2 tbsp of corn starch and 1 tsp of vanilla extract)
instructions: In a saucepan over low heat, melt the butter with honey, canola oil, and dark chocolate. Stir until smooth.
Remove from heat, then add the oats, sunflower seeds, walnuts, cocoa powder, and beaten egg. Mix until fully combined.
Press mixture firmly into a parchment-lined 8x8 inch pan. Chill for 15 minutes.
In a bowl, cream the butter until light. Add maple syrup and custard powder. Beat until smooth and fluffy.
Spread evenly over the chilled base. Return to the fridge for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle the finely chopped chocolate evenly on top of the middle layer

value.name: Pea Soup (Québécois Style)
value.text: This soup recipe attempts to capture the key elements of traditional Québécois pea soup, which is an historic part of the Cuisine of Quebec. Although pea soup is present in many European cuisines, Québécois pea soup has several distinctions: the base employs a simple mirepoix of celery, carrot, and onion, only yellow split peas are used, the soup is seasoned with thyme, and when a meat is added, it is ham.

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4533616

ingredients: 2 ea. (1.5–2 lbs / 700–900 g) raw ham hocks, on the bone
2 cups (400 g) dried yellow split peas, soaked overnight and drained
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Drizzle of olive or canola oil
instructions: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Roast ham hocks 30–40 min until browned, turning once partway through.
In a large pot, combine roasted ham hocks, onion, carrot, celery, thyme, bay leaf, peppercorns, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer, skimming off any foam that rises to the top.
Simmer 2.5–3 hours until meat is tender and broth is flavorful.
Remove ham hocks and cool slightly. Remove skin, bone, and excess fat from ham; shred meat into bite-sized pieces.
Strain the broth and discard solids. You should have about 8 cups.
Return strained broth to pot, and add soaked split peas, diced onion, carrot, celery, garlic, and thyme leaves.
Bring to gentle simmer and cook 60–75 minutes until peas are very tender.
If using miso, dissolve paste in ½ cup hot broth (do not boil miso directly) and stir into soup.
Add shredded ham and simmer 10–15 minutes.
Add salt and black pepper to taste.
For rustic soup, leave as is. For creamier texture, blend ⅓–½ of the soup with an immersion blender and stir to combine.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Serve with crusty rye, sourdough, or brown bread and optional drizzle of olive oil, canola oil, or sprinkle of parsley.

value.name: Maple Butter Tart
value.text: Butter tarts are a traditional Canadian dessert with a flaky pastry shell and a rich, buttery sweetened filling that stays slightly runny in the centre. The tarts are baked in muffin tins, so each is an individual portion. This version uses maple syrup instead of corn syrup for a more complex, especially Canadian version.

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4587522

ingredients: 1 tbsp white or apple cider vinegar
½ cup chopped pecans, walnuts, hazelnuts, or butternuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 190 °C (375 °F).
Mix the flour, salt, and sugar in the bowl of a food processor.
Cut in the cold butter and mix with a series of short pulses, until the mixture resembles pea-meal. The crust will have a flakier texture if you avoid mixing the butter in too much.
Gradually pulse in ice water, 1 tbsp at a time, until the dough just holds together. You may not need all the water.
Divide into two discs, wrap in plastic, and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Roll the dough to ⅛ inch (3 mm) thick. Cut into 4 inch (10 cm) rounds.
Gently press each round into a cup of a non-stick muffin pan. Chill the pan chill while making the filling.
Cream the butter and brown sugar until smooth.
Whisk in the eggs until light and slightly frothy.
Stir in maple syrup, vanilla, vinegar, and salt. Mix until smooth, but not foamy.
Fill tart shells with the filling to about about two-thirds full.
Sprinkle a spoonful of chopped nuts over the top of each tart.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until the centre is gooey and slightly runny, which is the traditional Canadian style. If you prefer a firmer tart, cook for 20 minutes.
Let cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then carefully lift out and cool on a rack.

instructions: put flour, sugar and oats into a bowl
separate eggs, yellow can go into the bowl, whites into a different bowl
whisk egg whites
mix ingredients in the big bowl, add milk to get a smooth batter
add spices
carefully add the whisked egg whites
add generous amounts of fat or oil into a pan
according to how big you want your pancakes, put appropriate amounts batter into the pan and bake until they golden, flip at the appropriate time.

value.name: Turkey & Barley Cabbage Rolls with Fresh Dill
value.text: This recipe adapts the traditional cabbage roll (Holubtsi) into a dish using ingredients that are produced in Canada, with chewy, nutty barley instead of rice. This improves the nutritional content and reduces the glycemic index. This recipe also aims to reduce saturated fat by replacing the red meat in the filling with ground turkey. This recipe mirrors cabbage rolls popular in Canada's prairie provinces by using green cabbage and fresh dill as a seasoning.

images.alt: Turkey & Barley Cabbage Rolls with Fresh Dill

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4630352

ingredients: 2 cloves garlic, minced (or ½ tsp garlic powder)
¼ cup chopped fresh dill, loosely packed (plus extra for garnish)
1 can (796 mL) no-salt-added crushed or diced tomatoes
1 tsp maple syrup or brown sugar (optional) (optional)
instructions: Simmer barley in the broth until tender (about 30–40 minutes). Drain excess liquid if needed and set aside to cool.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Core the cabbage and place it in the pot. Simmer for 5–10 minutes, removing leaves as they soften. Reserve 10–12 large leaves for rolling.
In a large bowl, make the filling by combining the cooked barley, ground turkey, onion, garlic, egg, dill, salt, and pepper.

Spread a cabbage leaf out flat on a work surface. Place 2–3 tablespoons of filling near the base of each cabbage leaf. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly to enclose the filling. Repeat with the remaining filling and cabbage leaves.

Prepare the sauce by mixing the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, canola oil, paprika, and apple cider vinegar in a bowl or large measuring cup. Add a the sugar or maple syrup if you like your sauces a bit sweeter.

Spread a few spoonfuls of the sauce on the bottom of a large baking dish or pot. Arrange the cabbage rolls over the tomatoes, seam-side down. Pour the rest of the sauce over top of the rolls Sprinkle with extra dill if desired.
For the oven method, cover with foil and bake at 175 °C (350 °F) for 1 hour. For the stovetop method, simmer gently, covered, on low heat for 1 hour.

value.name: Chilli Oil
value.text: This recipe is used to make chilli oil, an extremely useful and tasty condiment.

instructions: Mix chile flakes and salt in a heat-proof bowl.
Mix 1 tablespoon of the oil into the chile flake/salt mixture. This will prevent the chile from scorching when hot oil is added later.
Heat peanut oil to about 200°C (392°F). Small bubbles should form when poking a wooden chopstick into the oil.
Pour heated oil over chilli flake mixture and stir vigorously.
Allow to cool and store in a container.

value.name: Home Fries
value.text: Home Fries — a recipe imported from the Wikibooks Cookbook.

ingredients: 3 medium potatoes (e.g., russet or Yukon gold), peeled and diced
instructions: Boil diced potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes to soften slightly. Drain and let them dry.
Heat oil or butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add onions (and peppers if using), sauté until translucent.
Add the potatoes in a single layer. Let them brown undisturbed for 5–6 minutes.
Flip and cook the other sides until golden and crispy.
Season with salt, pepper, and paprika. Serve hot.

value.name: Orzo Salad
value.text: This pasta salad made with orzo is brightly flavored, lemon-forward, and colorful—perfect for anything from the dinner table to the picnic blanket.

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the turmeric.
Stir in the pasta, and boil until it is cooked to your taste.
Drain the pasta in a colander, and rinse briefly with cold water. Let drain.
Combine the capers, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, pepper and sugar in a jar. Seal the lid and shake well to combine and make the dressing.
Transfer the drained orzo to a large bowl, and pour the dressing over the pasta. Toss well to coat.
Add the parsley, sundried tomatoes, olives, and feta. Toss to combine.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

value.name: Kunun Aduwa (Nigerian Tiger Nut Milk)
value.text: Kunun aduwa is a traditional Nigerian beverage made from tiger nuts (Cyperus esculentus), known locally as aduwa. It is popular in Northern Nigeria and enjoyed for its natural sweetness and health benefits. The drink is creamy, refreshing, and often served cold.

ingredients: 2 cups dried or fresh tiger nuts (aduwa)
instructions: If using dried tiger nuts, soak them in water overnight to soften, then drain and rinse them.
In a blender, combine the tiger nuts, ginger, and dates. Blend until smooth and creamy, adding water as needed to aid blending.
Strain the blended mixture using a fine sieve or cheesecloth to separate the milk from the chaff.
Chill in the refrigerator and serve cold.

value.name: Omo tuo
value.text: Omo tuo is a rice dish that may have originated with the Hausa people and is still a favorite among Ghanaians today. To make it, rice is cooked and then rolled or pounded into balls, after which it is typically consumed with dried okro soup in northern Nigeria and with peanut or palm nut soup in Ghana.

instructions: After properly cleaning the rice, add it to a saucepan of water. When the rice is tender, add salt and bring to a boil. Give it a good five to seven minutes.
To make the rice smooth, mash it with a wooden spoon or a small pestle.
Pour cold water into a cup and place it near the pan. Transfer the rice to a serving dish after scooping it with wet hands and rolling it into balls.

value.name: Shitha
value.text: Shitha is a traditional spicy sauce commonly found in Arabian and Gulf cuisines, especially in countries like Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar. It is typically served as a condiment with rice dishes such as kabsa and mandi.

attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4524417

ingredients: 2 tablespoons red chile powder (or fresh red chilies, blended)
instructions: Heat the oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and sauté until golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften.
Add chile powder and salt. Stir well.
Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the mixture thickens.
Add lemon juice or vinegar if desired for extra tanginess.
Let it cool before serving.

value.name: Kunun kanwa
value.text: Kunun Kanwa is a traditional Hausa beverage made from grains and alkaline water (kanwa – potash or local salt). It is mostly consumed in Northern Nigeria, especially during cold weather or as a soothing drink for nursing mothers. It is smooth, warm, and slightly salty in taste.

wikibooks.note: Traditional Hausa warm drink made with grain flour and potash

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4526641

ingredients: 1 cup of guinea corn (or millet, sorghum, or maize) – ground into flour
1/2 teaspoon of edible potash (kanwa) or a small piece dissolved in water
1 small piece of ginger, peeled and grated
4-5 cups of water (adjust for desired consistency)
1–2 tablespoons of sugar or honey (optional, to taste)
instructions: Mix the Grain flour with a little water to form a light, smooth paste. Ensure there are no lumps.
In a separate pot, dissolve the kanwa (potash) in water and bring to a light boil.
Gradually pour the boiling kanwa water into the grain paste while stirring continuously.
Keep stirring until the mixture thickens slightly into a pap-like consistency.
Allow it to simmer for 2–3 minutes. Add more water if it's too thick.
Remove from heat. Add sugar or honey if desired.
Serve hot.

value.name: Faten Wake (Hausa Bean Porridge)
value.text: Faten wake is a traditional Hausa bean porridge from Northern Nigeria. This hearty and nutritious dish is made with soft-cooked beans, vegetables, and spices, and it is typically served as a main meal for lunch or dinner. It can be enjoyed on its own or with sides like bread, fried plantains, or pap.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4524793

ingredients: 2 cups dried beans (black-eyed peas or brown beans)
1–2 Scotch bonnet chiles or chile powder to taste
1–2 tablespoons groundnut oil or palm oil
1 small bunch of leafy greens, such as spinach, sorrel, ugu, amaranth, or bitterleaf, chopped (optional) (optional)
instructions: Rinse the beans thoroughly, removing any dirt or stones.
Place the beans in a pot, cover with enough water, and simmer over medium heat until soft and the water is almost absorbed (about 40–60 minutes).
Add chopped onions, tomatoes, chile, and oil to the cooked beans. Stir and allow to simmer for 10–15 minutes, until the mixture thickens and the flavors combine.
Stir in chopped leafy vegetables, ground crayfish, seasoning cubes, and salt. Continue cooking for another 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally until the porridge thickens and is well blended.
Serve hot.

value.name: User:Bamjos/Cornchaff Recipe
value.text: Corn chaff is corn and beans that is slowly simmered together with onions, tomatoes, red oil and other various spices.

ingredients: 2 cups dried corn (or 4 cups of pre-cooked corn)
1 cup palm oil (or more if desired)
3 seasoning cubes (Maggi, Knorr, etc) or 2 teaspoons bouillon seasoning powder
instructions: Boil your corn till it is soft, then , boil the beans till it is really soft.
Rinse out your corn if canned or frozen and set aside
Rinse out your beans then combine corn and bring in a pot with a cup of water and heat it
Prepare all your spices: ginger, garlic, onions, herbs, blend them together and add it to what you are cooking.
Add in salt, maggi and the palm oil.
Leave for about 20 minutes.

value.name: South African Curry and Rice
value.text: South African curry and rice is a combination dish of slow-cooked beef mince in a sweet and spicy curry sauce, served with basmati rice.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4525293

ingredients: 4 large carrots, peeled and chopped fine
2 cups fruit chutney (or less, if you want it less saucy)
A few sprigs fresh rosemary, chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add onion and garlic, then cook until translucent, without letting it brown or burn.
Add the meat and cook until browned.
Add the water, and bring the mixture to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots, and boil for another 10 minutes until the carrots and potatoes are softened.
Combine the tomato sauce, vinegar, sugar, curry powder, turmeric, flour, salt, and chutney in a mixing bowl. Mix it well.
Stir the sauce into the meat mixture, along with the rosemary. Cook for another 10–15 minutes.
Serve with the rice, chutney, coconut, and bananas.

value.name: Ofe Onugbu (Bitter Leaf Soup)
value.text: Ofe onugbu, or bitterleaf soup, is a traditional Nigerian soup commonly eaten by the Igbo people of Eastern Nigeria. It is prepared with thoroughly washed bitter leaves, meat, palm oil, local spices, and a thickener such as cocoyam, achi, or ofor. The soup is known for its rich flavor and slightly bitter taste. Serve with a swallow, such as pounded yam, eba (garri), or wheat meal.

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4523757

ingredients: 300 g assorted meat (beef, tripe, cow skin)
1 tablespoon ogiri or iru (fermented locust beans, optional)
3–5 small cocoyam pieces or 2 tablespoons achi powder (as thickener)
instructions: Wash the bitter leaves thoroughly, squeezing and rinsing several times to reduce the bitterness. Set aside.
In a pot, combine the assorted meat, stockfish, dryfish, salt, seasoning cubes, and chopped onions. Cover with water, and simmer until the meat is tender.
Add palm oil and allow it to melt into the meat stock.
If using cocoyam, boil it separately, peel, blend into a paste, and stir into the soup as a thickener. If using achi or ofor powder, stir directly into the pot.
Stir in the ground crayfish, pepper, ogiri, and ground crayfish.
Stir in the washed bitter leaves.Allow to simmer for 5–10 minutes until the soup thickens and the flavors combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

value.name: Zimbabwean Chicken and Vegetable Soup
value.text: Zimbabwean chicken and vegetable soup is a delicious soup that combines a variety of vegetables with peanut butter and a few red pepper flakes.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4521020

ingredients: 2 cups canned diced tomatoes, with juices
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, or more to taste
1 cup chopped cooked chicken, or to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion, and sauté for about 5 minutes until translucent.
Stir ½ cup of the vegetable stock and the peanut butter into the onions until the mixture looks smooth.
Stir in the remaining vegetable stock, diced tomatoes with their liquid, and crushed red pepper flakes; simmer for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in the cabbage, sweet potato, carrot, and turnip. Simmer, stirring, until the vegetables become soft (about 30 minutes).
Stir in the okra and chicken, and simmer for about 30 additional minutes.

value.name: Potato and Leek Soup II
value.text: This recipe for potato leek soup is adapted from one by Daisy Garnett in her book Cooking Lessons. It makes a creamy puréed soup whose texture is even smoother when sieved.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4526000

ingredients: 930 g leeks (not including the toughest portion of their green tops), halved lengthwise and sliced
600 g yellow potatoes, peeled and diced into 1–2 cm cubes
instructions: After preparing the leeks, wash them very well in water to remove all traces of dirt and grit, which hide between the layers. Drain well.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the vegetables, and season with a pinch each of salt and pepper. Stir to coat everything well with butter.
Cover the pot, and let the vegetables sweat over low heat for 10 minutes—make sure not to let them brown.
Stir in the chicken stock, and bring the pot to a boil. Simmer until the vegetables are cooked through.
Working in batches if necessary, purée the mixture using a hand- or full-size blender.
If you would like a very smooth soup, work the puréed mixture through a sieve into a clean pot—this is laborious, but it yields a velvety product.
Taste the soup, and season to taste with additional salt and pepper.

value.name: Chakalaka (South African Vegetable Stew)
value.text: Chakalaka is a spicy South African vegetable relish made from beans, peppers, carrots, and tomatoes. It is often served as a side dish with bread, pap (maize porridge), or meat. Chakalaka is versatile and can be customized with various vegetables and spices depending on regional or personal preference.

credit.artist: philipp from cape town, south africa

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4524693

ingredients: 1 teaspoon curry powder, or to taste
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and sauté for 2–3 minutes until softened.
Stir in the curry powder, chile powder, and chopped chile peppers. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes, grated carrots, and diced bell peppers. Stir well.
Add the crumbled bouillon cube and water. Cover and simmer for 10–15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the baked beans and cook for an additional 3–5 minutes, uncovered, until the mixture thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

value.name: Pumpkin Soufflé Casserole
value.text: This recipe for pumpkin soufflé casserole is adapted from one posted on Allrecipes.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4595937

ingredients: 1 pinch ground cinnamon, or more to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450 °F (230 °C), and grease the baking dish.
Use the electric mixer to beat together sugar, butter, and eggs until smooth and creamy.
Mix in pumpkin purée until well combined.
Add milk, cake flour, and baking powder, and mix until smooth.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish, and sprinkle cinnamon over top.
Bake in the heated oven until it is set in the middle, 45 minutes or more.

value.name: Tomato Bredie
value.text: Tomato bredie is a South African meal and it is good during the winter fare. Tomato Bredie is an old Cape name for a dish of meat and vegetables stewed together.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4573208

ingredients: 3½ pounds lamb or mutton breast chops, chopped into portions
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat oil in a large, heavy-bottomed saucepan
Dredge lamb in flour; shake off excess.
Then, cook the lamb in hot oil until it is brown. pour lamb into a plate, and reserve drip in the pan.

Cook and stir onion in drippings until soft for like 5 minutes, then mix tomatoes with it, return lamb chops to the saucepan; season with bay leaves, salt, brown sugar, black pepper, Worcestershire sauce, white peppercorns and bouillon, cover it, reduce the heat and simmer it for 1 hour and 15 minutes. Stir occasionally so that it wont sticks to the bottom of the pan.
Stir in potatoes; continue cooking until potatoes are cooked and meat is tender, about 45 minutes more.

value.name: Portuguese Sweet Rolls
value.text: Portuguese sweet rolls are soft, slightly sweet, lemon-scented dinner rolls. This recipe is a variation on a recipe by the same name from The King Arthur Flour Baker's Companion (2003 edition), and the easy yeast dough is a suitable yeast bread project for beginners.

license.attribution: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0)

attribution.name: Wikibooks Cookbook
attribution.notes: Text under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Wikibooks Cookbook contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (older revisions in the page history remain CC BY-SA 3.0). Source: https://en.wikibooks.org/w/index.php?oldid=4519635

ingredients: Potato flour is a fine powder made by drying and grinding white potatoes. It is useful for keeping bread doughs soft and baked goods moist longer. If you don't have any, then you can substitute unflavored instant mashed potato flakes (same weight, which is a much bigger volume), cornstarch (same volume), or plain all-purpose flour (same volume).

Vanilla extract is called for, but you can use whatever style of vanilla flavoring you have on hand. Two teaspoons of vanilla extract is a moderately large amount of vanilla (twice what you would put in a typical batch of cookies), so you may need to use a larger than usual amount of vanilla sugar, vanilla paste, etc.

Lemon oil is not the same as lemon extract. Instead, it is a pure oil pressed out of the outer skin of a lemon. If you don't have it on hand, use 1 heaping teaspoon finely shredded lemon zest (not candied lemon peel), 1 teaspoon lemon extract, or 1 ounce (30 g) lemon juice (and then reduce the warm water by the same amount). If you have very strong lemon oil, you may prefer to measure it with an eye dropper instead of a measuring spoon; you'll need about 10–20 drops of oil.

For the warm water, ordinary hot water straight from the tap is fine. The water should be warm but definitely not boiling, so you don't accidentally cook the yeast in the mixing bowl. If you haven't got hot water, then cold water will work, but your raising time will be a little longer.
instructions: Put flour, salt, sugar, potato flour, yeast, and butter into a mixing bowl. If you are using a stand mixer, fit the dough hook and turn the mixer to its lowest setting to begin stirring the ingredients together. If you are mixing by hand, give it a few strokes with a mixing spoon or spatula. The purpose of this step is to mostly distribute the yeast throughout the flour and other ingredients. Don't bother stirring it more than necessary for this step.
Mix the liquid ingredients together. Pour the liquid ingredients into the flour mixture.

Stir everything thoroughly. If you are using a stand mixer, let it run until the dough comes together. This will probably take several minutes. At first, it may look like it will never come together, and then it will suddenly form into a smooth ball, or even into a wet, slack batter. If you are mixing by hand, you can turn the dough out onto a clean, flat surface (can be oiled or floured, as you prefer) and knead the dough by hand for up to 10 minutes, adding flour or water by the spoonful as you feel the need.

Assess the texture of the dough. If the dough seems sticky (e.g., makes a sticky mess on your fingers) and is too slack to form into a smooth, soft ball, then you need to add more flour. Start with a generous spoonful, and stir again until it is incorporated. Repeat the addition as many times as necessary (it is unlikely that you will need to add more than about ½ cup/60 g of flour). If instead there is dry flour in the bottom, then pour a small spoonful of warm water directly on that dry part, and mix again until the dry flour and the water have been thoroughly incorporated. If you overcorrected, then add a spoonful of flour until you get a workable texture.
Unless it's a hot day, turn on the empty, cold oven for one minute. Then turn the oven off. The purpose of this short "preheating" is to make a comfortably warm place for the dough to rise.
Cover the dough to keep the surface from drying out. You can do this by coating the surface of the dough with oil, or by putting a lid or a big plate over the top of the mixing bowl.
Put the bowl of dough in the (now slightly warm) oven or another warm place. Double check that the oven has been turned off.
Let the dough rise for about 1 hour, until clearly puffy and almost twice the original volume. If you used cold water, it will take longer.
If you're using parchment paper, place a piece of parchment on your baking sheet. Otherwise, you can lightly grease the pan to keep the buns from sticking.
Sprinkle a big spoonful of flour on your work surface, and spread this out a bit.
Remove the bowl of dough from the oven. Scrape the puffy dough onto your floured work surface.

Roll the dough in the flour to lightly coat all sides with the flour. If needed, put more flour on your work surface to keep it from sticking. Roll the dough into a rough log shape. Use a sharp knife or a bench scraper to cut the dough into about 16 pieces of similar size.

Pick up one piece. Dust the wet edges in the remaining flour on your work surface, so it won't stick to your fingers. Choose one of the smoother sides of that piece to be the "top" of your roll. Grab the edges around your chosen "top" surface, and stretch or pinch them back to the "bottom". This has the effect of stretching the smooth side and hiding any lumpy bits on the bottom. Pinch the lumpy bits together on the bottom. Flatten the bun between your hands, and put it pinched-side-down on your baking sheet.

Repeat this for the other 15 pieces of dough, until all of the pieces are shaped. When you place the rolls on the baking sheet, leave about an inch or two in between them, so they have room to grow in the oven.

Place the baking sheet with the shaped buns back in the barely warm oven. Leave it there for about 45 minutes or an hour to proof. If your oven has cooled off while you were shaping the buns, you can warm it up again for 30 seconds or so, but be sure to turn it off before you put the pan of raw dough in the oven.
When the buns look nicely puffy, take the baking sheet of raw dough out of the oven.
Preheat the empty oven to 325 °F (165 °C, gas mark 3, moderately slow/warm).

When it is hot, put the proofed buns in the oven and bake for about 20 minutes. Cover them lightly with a piece of aluminum foil to prevent overbrowning, and then bake another 10 minutes (total of 30 minutes in the oven). If you are using a thermometer to check the internal temperature, aim for 190 °F (88 °C).
Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature with butter and jam. Alternatively, slice them in half and use them for sandwiches.

value.name: Luciabullar (Scandinavian Saffron Buns)
value.text: Lussekatter or luciabullar are Scandinavian saffron buns served on St. Lucia Day (13 December).
