funFacts.text: Buffalo wings were invented in 1964 at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York, when Teressa Bellissimo fried up wings as a late-night snack.

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

instructions: Pat wings dry and toss with baking powder and salt.
Arrange on a rack; optionally dry uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Bake low, then increase heat to crisp the skin fully.
Warm hot sauce with butter (and a little sugar) into a glossy Buffalo sauce.
Toss baked wings in sauce and serve with blue cheese dip and celery.

value.name: Tacos al Pastor
value.text: Pork marinated in a bright adobo of guajillo chiles, achiote, citrus and spices, roasted or grilled and served on corn tortillas with charred pineapple, onion and cilantro — a Mexico City classic with roots in Lebanese shawarma.

funFacts.text: 'Al pastor' means 'shepherd style' — the spit-roasted pork technique came from Lebanese immigrants' shawarma, adapted with Mexican chilis.

attribution.name: Isabel Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

instructions: Soften dried chiles in hot water.
Blend chiles with achiote, citrus, vinegar, garlic and spices into a marinade.
Marinate the sliced pork several hours or overnight.
Roast, grill or broil the pork until cooked and caramelized; grill pineapple.
Chop pork and pineapple; serve on warm corn tortillas with onion, cilantro and lime.

value.name: Mango Sticky Rice
value.text: Warm glutinous rice steeped in sweet-salty coconut milk, served with slices of ripe mango and a drizzle of salted coconut sauce and crispy mung beans.

credit.artist: Dennis Wong from Hong Kong, Hong Kong

funFacts.text: Thailand's beloved 'khao niao mamuang' peaks in the hot season, when mangoes are ripe and paired with coconut-soaked glutinous rice.

attribution.name: Hot Thai Kitchen
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

instructions: Soak sticky rice, then steam until tender and translucent.
Warm coconut milk with sugar and salt (do not boil hard).
Pour most of the sweet coconut mixture over the hot rice; mix and rest covered.
Make a thicker salted coconut sauce for topping.
Serve rice with sliced mango, salted coconut sauce and crispy mung beans.

value.name: Chicken Biryani
value.text: Spiced yogurt-marinated chicken layered with par-cooked basmati rice, fried onions and saffron, then steamed (dum) so the rice absorbs the aromatic curry beneath.

funFacts.text: Biryani descends from Mughal-era layered rice dishes, finished with the sealed-pot 'dum' method that steams meat and rice together.

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

instructions: Marinate chicken in spiced yogurt.
Fry onions until golden and crisp; reserve.
Par-boil basmati rice with whole spices; drain.
Cook the marinated chicken into a thick curry base in a heavy pot.
Layer par-cooked rice over the chicken with fried onions, herbs and saffron.
Drizzle ghee, cover tightly and steam (dum) on low heat.
Rest, then gently fold and serve.

value.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
value.text: Chargrilled yogurt-marinated chicken folded into a deeply spiced, creamy tomato-onion gravy — the celebrated British-Indian dish with a smoky edge, most often credited to Glasgow's Shish Mahal.

funFacts.text: Widely believed to have been invented in Britain (Glasgow, 1970s); in 2001 a UK foreign secretary called it 'a true British national dish.'

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

ingredients: Garam masala, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, chili
instructions: Marinate chicken in spiced yogurt.
Chargrill or broil chicken until charred at the edges.
Cook onion, ginger and garlic; add ground spices.
Add tomato passata and simmer into a thick sauce.
Blend sauce smooth if desired; stir in cream.
Add grilled chicken; simmer briefly and serve.

value.name: Butter Chicken
value.text: Yogurt-and-spice marinated chicken simmered in a velvety tomato sauce mellowed with butter and cream, fragrant with garam masala, cumin and turmeric.

funFacts.text: Born at Delhi's Moti Mahal in the 1950s, when cooks simmered leftover tandoori chicken in a buttery tomato gravy to keep it from drying out.

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

ingredients: Garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, cumin
instructions: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger, garlic, lemon and spices.
Sear or grill the marinated chicken.
Sauté onion in butter; add spices and tomato passata.
Simmer until the sauce deepens in color and thickens.
Stir in cream and the cooked chicken; simmer to combine.
Finish with butter; serve with rice or naan.

value.name: Coq au Vin
value.text: Bone-in chicken marinated and braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and onions until the meat is succulent and the sauce is dark, glossy and rich.

funFacts.text: The dish was designed to tenderize a tough old rooster ('coq') by long, slow braising in acidic red wine.

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

instructions: Marinate chicken overnight in red wine with onion and herbs.
Strain and reserve wine; pat chicken dry.
Reduce the wine by half on the stove.
Cook bacon until golden; sauté chicken, mushrooms and onions separately.
Combine with reduced wine and stock; braise about 45 minutes.
Thicken sauce with a butter-flour paste; season and serve.

value.name: Beef Bourguignon
value.text: The king of French stews: beef and bacon lardons slow-braised in red Burgundy with carrots, then finished with buttery sautéed mushrooms and pearl onions.

funFacts.text: A rustic Burgundy peasant stew for tenderizing tough beef, later elevated to haute cuisine by chef Auguste Escoffier.

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

instructions: Brown bacon lardons; render fat and set aside.
Sear beef in batches until well browned.
Sauté onion and carrot; stir in tomato paste and flour.
Deglaze with red wine; add stock, garlic and herbs.
Braise low and slow (oven or stovetop) until beef is fork-tender.
Separately sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in butter; stir in.
Adjust sauce thickness and seasoning; rest, ideally overnight.

value.name: Greek Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki
value.text: Chicken marinated in olive oil, lemon, garlic and oregano, threaded on skewers and grilled, then tucked into warm pita with cool cucumber-yogurt tzatziki.

funFacts.text: 'Souvlaki' means 'little skewer' — Greeks have grilled meat on skewers since antiquity (charred skewer sets survive from the Bronze Age).

attribution.name: The Mediterranean Dish
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

ingredients: 2 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into pieces
1 tsp each salt and black pepper
Sliced tomato, cucumber, onion, Kalamata olives
instructions: Blend garlic, oregano, rosemary, paprika, salt, pepper, olive oil, wine and lemon juice into a marinade.
Toss chicken with marinade and bay leaves; refrigerate 2 hours to overnight.
Soak wooden skewers; thread chicken.
Grill skewers, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm pita; assemble with tzatziki, chicken and vegetables.

value.name: Moussaka
value.text: Layers of tender eggplant and a cinnamon-scented tomato beef (or lamb) sauce under a thick blanket of baked béchamel — Greece's answer to lasagna.

funFacts.text: The béchamel-topped moussaka Greeks know today was created in the 1920s by French-trained chef Nikolaos Tselementes.

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

instructions: Slice and roast (or fry) the eggplant until softened.
Cook onion, garlic and mince; add tomato, wine and spices and simmer into a thick sauce.
Make a béchamel with butter, flour and milk; whisk in egg yolks and cheese off heat.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish.
Top with béchamel and bake until golden.
Rest before slicing.

value.name: Spaghetti Carbonara
value.text: A Roman classic of hot spaghetti bound in a glossy, cheese-and-egg sauce enriched with crisp rendered guanciale and lots of cracked black pepper — no cream.

funFacts.text: Carbonara's origin is fiercely debated; the best-supported theory ties it to 1944 Rome, marrying local pasta with American ration bacon and eggs.

attribution.name: Serious Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

ingredients: 1/2 cup diced guanciale, pancetta or bacon
1/4 cup grated Pecorino Romano, plus more for serving
1/4 cup grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, plus more for serving
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper, plus more for serving
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil; cook spaghetti until al dente, reserving pasta water.
Cook guanciale with 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat until fat renders and it crisps.
Whisk eggs, yolks, both cheeses and black pepper in a large heatproof bowl.
Set bowl over the pasta pot as a double boiler (or off heat) and add hot drained pasta.
Toss, adding reserved pasta water gradually, until a creamy sauce forms.
Stir in the guanciale; serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

value.name: Pad Thai
value.text: Springy rice noodles tossed in a sweet-sour tamarind sauce with fish sauce and palm sugar, scrambled egg, tofu and chicken, finished with crushed peanuts, bean sprouts and a squeeze of lime.

funFacts.text: Pad Thai was promoted by the Thai government in the 1930s-40s to build national identity and cut rice consumption during hard times.

attribution.name: RecipeTin Eats
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

ingredients: 150 g chicken breast or thigh, thinly sliced
1/2 cup firm tofu, cut into batons
1/4 cup garlic chives, cut into pieces
instructions: Soak rice noodles in room-temperature water until pliable; drain.
Mix tamarind, fish sauce, oyster sauce and brown sugar into a sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat; cook garlic and onion briefly.
Add chicken and tofu; cook until chicken is nearly done.
Push to one side, scramble the eggs, then combine.
Add drained noodles and sauce; toss until noodles absorb sauce.
Add bean sprouts, garlic chives and most of the peanuts; toss briefly.
Serve topped with remaining peanuts, chili and lime wedges.

value.name: Greek Cucumber Tomato Feta Salad
value.text: A bright summer side: crisp cucumber, sweet cherry tomatoes, and salty feta tossed with parsley in a garlicky oregano and red-wine vinaigrette. Ready in minutes, better after a rest in the fridge, and it keeps for about five days.

funFacts.text: 'Horiatiki' means 'village salad' — authentically it has no lettuce and is crowned with a whole slab of feta.

attribution.name: Erin Lives Whole (Erin Antoniak)
attribution.notes: Ingredients and method adapted from the source; description rewritten.

ingredients: 2 pints cherry or grape tomatoes, halved
instructions: Chop and prepare the vegetables, feta, and parsley.
Combine the cucumber, tomatoes, feta, and parsley in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil, vinegar, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper; toss until everything is evenly coated.
Serve right away, or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days.
